title: The salt run
prompt:
Create an eight-second cinematic sequence from an original desert adventure film. A battered mustard-yellow rally coupe escapes a narrow red-rock canyon and bursts onto an immense pale salt basin. The miniature story is confinement, a sudden opening, then release. This is finished narrative cinema: physical locations, purposeful coverage, a consistent vehicle and a decisive final composition. Deliver three distinct shots with hard cuts motivated by the car's movement. The frame is landscape 16:9 throughout, filled edge to edge.

VISUAL WORLD AND CONTINUITY
Late afternoon after a dry storm. Copper sandstone walls stand against a pale cyan sky; low sunlight enters the canyon from the left and catches suspended ochre dust. Keep natural shadow detail and bright sunlit rock, with restrained photochemical grain and a gentle highlight shoulder. The same unbranded two-door coupe appears in every shot: mustard-yellow body, matte charcoal bonnet, two round headlights, black wheels, a compact roof rack holding one strapped spare tyre. Glass is dusty and reflections remain physical. The driver is only a dark figure behind the windscreen; no facial close-up or dialogue is needed. Preserve wheelbase, panel shapes, wheel count, rack and paint across cuts. The road has a firm sandy surface, scattered pebbles and one broad right-hand curve. Dust must originate from contact with the tyres and trail behind the car; it does not materialise in front.

SHOT 1 — 00:00–00:02 — THE CHASE IS ALREADY MOVING
Low tracking three-quarter view from ahead and to the car's left, approximately 35 mm spherical lens, camera about half a metre above the ground. The coupe advances fast from left towards right through the narrow canyon, its front suspension visibly compressing once over a shallow rut. A near rock edge passes in the foreground; the camera travels with the vehicle, so the coupe remains legible while the canyon streaks with natural directional motion blur. The road opens towards a bright gap ahead. This is a controlled vehicle-rig shot, not an orbit around a parked car. Cut as the front wheel reaches the curve.

SHOT 2 — 00:02–00:03 — TRACTION
A brief low close insert of the left rear wheel and lower yellow body, approximately 75 mm lens. The tyre bites into the sandy bend and throws a fan of small stones backwards; the rear suspension loads and settles. The wheel rotates naturally and remains attached to the axle. Keep the same left-to-right travel and sunlight direction. This one-second insert provides physical punctuation, not a separate event or an advertisement. Cut on the grit leaving the tyre.

SHOT 3 — 00:03–00:08 — THE WORLD OPENS
Wide elevated three-quarter tracking shot, approximately 28 mm lens, looking diagonally through the canyon mouth towards the salt basin. The same coupe exits the shade and follows the sweeping curve from the lower left towards the bright open distance on the right. The camera rises smoothly a few metres while easing back, revealing the immense flat white basin and a dark storm front on the distant horizon. Let the dust trail curl along the car's actual path. At the end the car is still moving, small but clearly visible against the basin; the landscape owns the frame. Give this reveal time to breathe rather than inserting more cuts.

FINISH AND SOUND
Real-time motion with a coherent 24 fps cinematic shutter impression. Stable terrain and convincing scale, weighted suspension, continuous travel across each cut, no teleporting vehicle or speed ramps. Preserve the three-shot progression; no dissolves, split screens, titles, subtitles, logos or black bars. Native sound is purely diegetic: engine load, gravel spray and dry wind, with the same engine note carried across the insert and widening naturally in the final shot. No speech, voice-over or music. The result must remain visually intelligible when muted.

title: The rising sea
prompt:
Create an eight-second sequence from an original maritime adventure film. A small steel research vessel climbs a steep ocean swell, disappears briefly behind wind-torn spray, then emerges on the far shoulder of the wave. Tell one physical event in three shots: approaching mass, impact, regained momentum. The sequence should feel photographed from real marine camera rigs, with a powerful but readable sea rather than a wall of abstract particles. Landscape 16:9, full frame throughout.

ART DIRECTION
Cold turquoise Atlantic water under an immense overcast sky. A break in the clouds sends clean afternoon light from the upper left, revealing white foam and the warm rust of the ship's bow. There is brightness and colour within the storm; retain detail in hull, sea and sky. The vessel is a compact, approximately twenty-metre research boat with a dark navy hull, weathered white wheelhouse, burnt-orange bow rail, one rear antenna mast and a small yellow lifebuoy fixed to the port railing. There are no readable names or logos. Keep this construction identical between shots. A tiny crew silhouette can be visible behind the wheelhouse glass, but the story is the ship meeting the sea, not a performance to camera.

PHYSICAL RULES
The swell travels towards the boat; the boat advances consistently from left to right. A broad sloping wave face lifts the bow before the hull settles over the crest. Water wraps around the hull and breaks away in sheets, then droplets; foam follows surface currents. The ship has weight, buoyancy and inertia, with a plausible pitch and only a restrained roll. The hull never bends, splits, transforms or floats above the water. Keep the horizon, wave direction, daylight and wind direction consistent across the edit.

SHOT 1 — 00:00–00:03 — THE CLIMB
Wide water-level three-quarter view from the port side, approximately 40 mm lens. The navy vessel advances left to right into a rising turquoise swell. The camera moves alongside, slightly lower than the orange bow rail; foreground water swells past the lens but never entirely hides the action. Over these three seconds the bow rises and the dark hull becomes more visible, emphasizing the gradient of the wave. White foam catches the raking light. The frame retains enough sky for the audience to understand the tilt. Cut at the first hard burst of spray over the bow.

SHOT 2 — 00:03–00:04 — CONTACT
One-second close detail from just behind the port bow rail, approximately 65 mm lens. A heavy sheet of water strikes the fixed orange rail and breaks into sharply lit droplets. The same chipped paint and weathered bolts remain visible through the water. The camera is attached to the ship and moves with its restrained pitch; the distant horizon dips accordingly. Keep this a forceful single event with real water weight, not slow-motion decorative mist. The impact is the reason for the cut.

SHOT 3 — 00:04–00:08 — THROUGH
Cut to a wider, slightly elevated 32 mm view from the same side of the action axis. For the first fraction of the shot, drifting spray partly obscures the bow. As it falls, the vessel crests the swell and drives down the far shoulder, still left to right. The camera tracks with it, allowing the next rolling wave and a distant sunlit strip of sea to appear behind. The ship returns towards level as foam streams along its hull. End on forward movement and an open route through the water, not an unexplained freeze or a sinking ship. Hold this final composition long enough to feel the scale.

CINEMATOGRAPHY AND SOUND
Naturalistic maritime photography with rich cyan water, off-white foam, rusty orange accents, soft highlight roll-off and restrained texture. Photographic depth and occasional realistic spray near the lens; no artificial lens flare, game-render gloss or gratuitous camera spins. Real-time motion; three hard cuts as specified, with action continuity across them. Native sound: wind, the heavy impact of water, a low engine vibration carried continuously through the cuts, then water draining off the bow. No intelligible speech, score, trailer hits, titles or captions. The sequence must tell its story silently as well.

title: Above the city
prompt:
Create an eight-second, three-shot sequence from an original retro-futurist cinematic thriller, composed specifically for portrait 9:16. A narrow industrial exterior lift carries a lone maintenance engineer upward through a dense city canyon. It passes out of cool shadow into warm dawn and reveals an immense sunlit skyline above the low cloud. The story is ascent and discovery, told through space, machinery and light. This is a vertical cinema frame, not a cropped landscape film, not UGC and not a person addressing the viewer.

WORLD, MATERIALS AND COMPOSITION
Build a believable future city from weathered stone towers, bronze structural ribs, ribbed glass and external lift shafts. Avoid generic neon cyberpunk. The lower city is cool and misty; morning sunlight warms the upper architecture to honey, copper and pale gold. The lift is an open-sided maintenance platform inside a rigid metal cage, with a waist-high dark railing, one amber work lamp and two parallel steel guide rails anchored to the facade. A single adult male engineer stands securely behind the railing in an ochre work coat, dark trousers and a compact grey harness. His face is not the subject. Keep his clothing, the cage structure and the lamp unchanged across shots.
Use the tall frame intentionally: machinery and foreground mass at the bottom, the lift in the central axis, architecture and the destination climbing into the top. Perspective and occlusion must describe a real vertical journey. No horizontal letterboxing, phone interface or decorative frame.

SHOT 1 — 00:00–00:02 — SOMETHING RISES
A low, nearly upward-looking 24 mm shot from inside the city canyon. The maintenance lift climbs from the lower third towards the centre along the building's two straight rails. The camera stays on a fixed neighbouring ledge and tilts upward modestly to follow; vertical lines remain coherent. A near bronze beam gives foreground depth. The engineer is a small silhouette, one hand resting on the railing. Distant mist reveals layers of towers. Establish real upward motion and the enormous height above before cutting to the mechanism.

SHOT 2 — 00:02–00:03 — THE MECHANISM
One-second close insert, approximately 65 mm lens, showing a steel guide wheel rolling upward against the same vertical rail. Worn metal, grease and a small bead of condensation catch the first warm light. A fixed bolt on the rail travels down through the frame as the lift rises, making direction unmistakable. The wheel rotates in the correct direction, the rail remains straight, and the background slides downward. This is the mechanical heartbeat of the ascent, not a floating object shot. Cut as the warm band of light crosses the wheel.

SHOT 3 — 00:03–00:08 — ABOVE THE CLOUD
View from just behind and to the side of the engineer on the moving platform, approximately 28 mm lens, still portrait. His coat and the amber lamp occupy the lower quarter while the rails lead upward along one edge. For the opening second, a heavy horizontal architectural ledge masks the skyline. The lift rises past that ledge naturally, revealing tiered towers emerging from a white cloud sea, and a huge warm rising sun partially veiled by haze. The camera makes a single gentle forward push within the platform, without flying through the engineer or railing. He turns his head slightly towards the view. The platform continues rising; the reveal settles into a luminous final composition with visible atmospheric layers and genuinely monumental scale. The last frame remains alive with drifting cloud and the machinery's subtle motion.

CONTINUITY AND FINISH
The same lift climbs continuously; no jump to a different building, duplicated engineer, changing rail geometry or impossible acceleration. Natural fabric response to the mild wind. Deep blacks remain open and the sunlit reveal is bright without clipping the cloud. Restrained fine grain, subtle optical softness at distant edges, convincing photographed production design. Use three clean hard cuts, no transitions, speed ramps, holographic text or montage of unrelated skylines. Native sound is spatial and understated: winch vibration, a short metal rattle at the insert, wind opening up as the platform emerges. No speech, narration, music, logos or captions. The image alone should deliver the emotional release.

title: The glass garden
prompt:
Create an eight-second cinematic passage from an original luminous fantasy adventure, designed natively for a tall 9:16 frame. Inside an enormous abandoned glasshouse, a closed ivory flower the size of a tree opens as the first sunlight reaches it. The unfurling canopy releases a small cloud of golden pollen and transforms the light in the chamber. Tell this one event through three connected shots: the arrival of light, a tactile sign of life, then the full revelation. The wonder comes from scale and plausible organic motion, not from a person speaking or a sequence of beauty portraits.

THE SET
A monumental nineteenth-century iron-and-glass conservatory, reclaimed by green ferns and climbing vines. Tall curved iron ribs rise towards a broken glass dome. Wet stone steps and a shallow reflecting pool fill the base of the scene. The giant flower grows from one thick green stem on a central island, its folded ivory petals bearing faint translucent veins and warm apricot edges. It has a clearly defined centre and six broad overlapping petals, all belonging to one stable plant. Tiny ordinary plants around its base provide scale. One distant explorer in a plain deep-blue coat stands motionless at the far side of the pool, only as a small scale cue; no facial coverage, dialogue or character performance is required. There are no signs, inscriptions or logos.

LIGHT AND TEXTURE
Early morning, fresh and luminous rather than dark or ominous. A shaft of warm sunlight enters from the upper right through a missing glass pane, touching moisture and pale dust in the air. Emerald foliage, aged iron, blue reflections and creamy petals create a rich natural palette. Show condensation, subtle water ripples and the fibrous translucency of the petals. Maintain photographic materials and spatial depth: the chamber should feel like a real large set with one extraordinary living plant, not a flat illustration or plastic animation.

SHOT 1 — 00:00–00:02 — LIGHT REACHES THE FLOWER
A symmetrical, low wide portrait composition on a 24 mm lens. The pool occupies the bottom quarter, the tightly folded flower stands in the middle, and the rising iron ribs and glass dome fill the upper half. Slowly push forward along the pool's edge as a thin cloud uncovers the sun, letting the warm beam grow across the plant. The flower's reflection trembles in a small existing ripple. Establish the intact room geometry, the same central plant and the small explorer behind it. Cut when sunlight reaches a folded petal seam.

SHOT 2 — 00:02–00:03 — THE FIRST MOVEMENT
A one-second close insert on a 90 mm macro lens: a dewdrop follows a vein down the warm ivory edge as the petal begins to separate from its neighbour. The petal flexes from its attached base with a slow, elastic organic motion; it does not dissolve or change material. The droplet falls out of frame under gravity. Backlight reveals the fine branching veins. The first opening is the visual cause of the next wide shot.

SHOT 3 — 00:03–00:08 — THE CANOPY WAKES
Cut to a low three-quarter wide view on a 28 mm lens, preserving the plant's location, pool and direction of sunlight. Over five seconds the same six petals unfurl outward and upward in a continuous coordinated motion, opening a vast ivory canopy inside the dome. The movement starts at each petal's attached base and propagates towards its edge; keep the stem rooted and the petal count stable. The camera tilts upward slowly, using the tall frame to follow the opening towards the roof. Near the end, a modest drifting cloud of golden pollen lifts into the sunlight above the flower, while its changing silhouette travels across the wet stone and water below. End on the fully opened canopy framed by the iron ribs, with room to read its enormous scale. No explosion of arbitrary particles or abrupt time-lapse.

EDITORIAL AND SOUND
Three motivated hard cuts with uneven durations; the final unfurling deserves the longest uninterrupted view. Natural 24 fps cinematic movement, fine texture, gentle highlight bloom only around the real sunbeam, no animated text, subtitles, title card or black bars. Preserve the flower, room, explorer and lighting axis across the edit. Native ambience is quiet: distant morning birds outside the dome, a soft breath of wind through leaves, the faint fall of the water drop. No voice, score or magical sound-effect crescendo. The visual progression must remain complete with the gallery muted.
